subject: Nuvera Health — private VPC custody, retention windows and deterministic wipe procedure
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nuvera.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@nuvera.com, security@nuvera.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: Nuvera private VPC custody, retention and deterministic wipe

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. We need to close out a handful of items before legal/procurement will sign: specifically around customer-controlled storage in the Private deployment and how you guarantee data residency and deletion. Attached is our security questionnaire but below are the immediate clarifications we need: 

1) In a Private/VPC deployment, what exactly lives in our VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane? We need a short custody map (snapshots, backups, logs).
2) Retention windows: if Nuvera requests an immediate erase of a tenant, what systems hold copies and what are the maximum windows before a deterministic wipe is complete?
3) Proof of deletion: can Redwood provide a signed attestation and an evidence package (tombstone manifest, snapshot hashes) we can store for audit?
4) Escrow/third-party verification: willing to accept an independent auditor to verify wipe completeness? If yes, what are the access requirements?

Can you respond in writing so we can attach answers to the questionnaire? Preferably by Monday.

Thanks,
Liam
Security Lead 
Nuvera Health

Attachment: nuvera-security-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nuvera.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: Nuvera private VPC custody, retention and deterministic wipe

Liam — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Dev (infra) and Grace (customer success) so we can give technical detail + operational next steps. High-level answers first; we'll follow with a technical appendix and a proposed mutual action plan.

High-level:
- Custody map: In Private mode the customer controls compute and persistent block/object storage in their VPC. Redwood runs a lightweight control plane (optional in-customer or hosted) that holds only metadata and orchestration state; no raw tenant data is stored in the hosted control plane unless you opt into remote backups.
- Retention & wipe: We support immediate tenant-triggered wipe. Typical deterministic wipe completes within 72 hours for primary storage and up to 7 days for immutable off-site backup snapshots depending on the configuration (we document the SLA options).
- Proof-of-delete: We can produce a signed attestation, a tombstone manifest (list of affected volumes/snapshots with SHA256 digests), and an audit log export. We also support an independent auditor review; see details below.

Next steps — Dev will drop the technical appendix with the exact procedures, command-level artifacts, log paths, and proof-of-delete format. Grace will propose a short MAP and suggested SLA language for procurement.

Best,
Soojin 
Head of Customer Security 
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nuvera.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: Nuvera private VPC custody, retention and deterministic wipe

Liam — capturing the technical appendix here. I'll keep it concise but include the artifacts you'll need for audit. Happy to expand on any item.

1) Custody map (Private deployment, default topology):
   - Customer VPC: block/object stores (EBS/S3 or equivalents), worker instances with ephemeral local cache, optional managed snapshot repo in your account.
   - Redwood control plane (hosted): orchestration metadata only (model routing, job ids). No customer tokens or raw data blobs are retained unless you enable remote backups to Redwood-managed storage.

2) Data copies and where they can live:
   - Primary data: resides only on volumes in your VPC.
   - Short-lived KV/prefix caches: in-memory on workers; KV caches are flushed on node restart and not tiled to long-term storage.
   - Point-in-time snapshots: if snapshot/backup is enabled, snapshots are stored in your account (preferred) or optionally in a Redwood-managed escrow bucket (customer must opt-in).
   - Logs and audit trails: application logs are written to a customer-configured logging sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk). We can retain a copy in the control plane for support incidents for up to 30 days with your consent.

3) Deterministic wipe procedure (tenant deletion request):
   Phase A — Initiation: Customer files delete request via the Console or API (DELETE /v1/tenants/{id}/wipe).
   Phase B — Quiesce: Active processing is drained; new writes are rejected.
   Phase C — Primary wipe: All block storage volumes attached to tenant instances are zeroed and deleted via provider-native secure-delete APIs where supported. We run a parallel verification job that computes SHA256 digests of pre-wipe and post-wipe tombstones for directories/snapshots.
   Phase D — Snapshot/backup purge: Any point-in-time snapshots in your account are deleted; for Redwood-managed escrow snapshots we run a final shred process followed by object-store garbage collection. Completion window: primary wipe typically within 24–72 hours; full purge including escrow snapshots and background garbage collection up to 7 days.

4) Proof-of-delete artifacts delivered:
   - Tombstone manifest (JSON): list of deleted objects/volumes + pre-deletion digests (SHA256) and deletion timestamps.
   - Signed attestation (PDF): Redwood security officer signs a time-stamped statement of completion with a UUID reference.
   - Audit log export: line-delimited logs of the wipe operation (start/finish/verification checks) including job ids.

5) Keys & encryption:
   - Customer-managed KMS (recommended): we do not hold key material. When tenant keys are revoked/destroyed in your KMS, data encrypted under those keys becomes inaccessible; we still provide tombstone manifests and logs.
   - Redwood-managed keys: if used, we provide a key-destruction certificate and timeline as part of the attestation.

6) Independent audit/escrow:
   - We support a one-time independent auditor engagement. Access required: read-only IAM role into your VPC storage, ability to inspect snapshots within a narrow time window, and escorted access to the Redwood-managed escrow bucket (if used). We can coordinate NDAs and scope.

7) Limitations & edge cases:
   - Immutable backups configured outside customer control may require longer GC windows in the object store provider; we enumerate those in the final SLA.
   - Air-gapped or offline cold-storage that sits off-provider will require manual deletion steps; we will capture those in the tombstone manifest.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-wipe-playbook-v1.md (markdown), proof-of-delete-attestation-template.pdf (application/pdf)

Let me know if you want the appendix expanded into a step-by-step runbook.

—Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nuvera.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement <procure@nuvera.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: Nuvera private VPC custody, retention and deterministic wipe

Thanks Dev — that's very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups before we present to procurement:

- Is the tombstone manifest itself signed/verifiable? We'd prefer the manifest include a signature block that we can verify independently (not just a Redwood-signed PDF).
- For the 24–72 hour primary wipe SLA, can you commit to a deterministic worst-case of 96 hours for the contract, with an operational target of 48? Procurement wants a hard ceiling.
- For escrow snapshots that Redwood may hold (if we opt in), can we require monthly automated delete sweeps until the tenant is destroyed (so objects don't linger)?

Also — procurement asked for a short flowchart or single-page summary we can attach to the contract. Can you produce a 1-page "wipe and evidence" summary (PDF) we can share?

If you can send the signed manifest template and the 1-pager by EOD Wednesday we can move to redlines.

Regards,
Liam

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nuvera.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: Nuvera private VPC custody, retention and deterministic wipe

Liam — great clarifying points. Commitments we can take into the contract negotiation: 

1) Manifest signature: we'll produce a machine-verifiable tombstone manifest signed with an X.509-based code-signing cert we own; we will also include an accompanying detached PGP signature if Nuvera prefers.
2) SLA ceiling: we can agree to a contractual worst-case completion time of 96 hours for primary wipe and full purge completion within 10 days for scenarios involving escrow snapshots (contract language to be precise). Operational targets will be 48 hours / 7 days respectively.
3) Escrow delete sweeps: we will implement an automated monthly sweep for escrow buckets post-termination and provide the sweep job logs as part of the attestation package.

Action items:
- Dev: produce the signed tombstone manifest template + detached PGP example and the single-page wipe/evidence PDF by EOD Wednesday (2025-07-09).
- Grace & Marissa: finalize MAP and proposed contract clauses for procurement (I'll attach the SLA language draft).
- Liam/procurement: confirm whether you want Redwood-managed escrow or customer-only snapshots (this changes the deletion window).

I'll attach the proposed one-pager and the playbook draft for you to review.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Soojin
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nuvera-wipe-one-pager.pdf (application/pdf); redwood-vpc-wipe-playbook-v1.md (markdown)
